newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bootleg liquor death toll rises to 27 in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Bootleg liquor death toll rises to 27 in Pakistan.

text.p: Twenty-seven people have died from drinking bootleg liquor in a city in Pakistan, where alcohol is banned for Moslems, doctors said on Tuesday.
They said the victims had arrived at Liaquat Medical College Hospital in the southern city of Hyderabad in critical condition on Sunday night and Monday with severe vomiting and diarrhoea.
Thirteen died on Monday, including the 25-year-old son of a deputy superintendent of police.
At first the victims were reluctant to admit that they had consumed illegally distilled liquor because Moslems caught drinking may be flogged under Pakistan's strict Islamic laws.
Violating the ban on alcohol is considered a more serious sin in the fasting month of Ramadan now under way.
Police said they had registered a case against the owner of the distillery that produced the poisonous brew.
